seams.why: Managed files must preserve ownership and use atomic replacement.
seams.remediation: Call config.WriteOwnedFileAtomic instead of os.Rename.

seams.why: One root resolver prevents environment spellings from selecting different repositories.
seams.remediation: Call buildinfo.ResolveSourceRoot instead of reading a root environment variable directly.

seams.why: A shared typed decoder preserves dependency defaults and forward compatibility.
seams.remediation: Call scenario.LoadServiceManifest instead of privately decoding service.json.

seams.why: The shared command boundary centralizes lookup, cancellation, and test injection.
seams.remediation: Use internal/shell instead of os/exec directly.

seams.why: Identity variables must be established as one coherent fixture so tests resolve the same home as production.
seams.remediation: Use internal/testenv instead of setting identity variables independently.

seams.why: Credential-store tests need one failure-injectable in-memory implementation so missing-value and backend-failure behavior cannot drift by package.
seams.remediation: Use testenv.NewCredentialStore instead of declaring a package-local credential store.

seams.why: A concurrency-safe shared clock keeps deterministic time advancement identical across package tests.
seams.remediation: Use testenv.NewClock instead of declaring a package-local fixed or test clock.

seams.why: CLI wire-contract tests need one typed decoder with consistent failure diagnostics.
seams.remediation: Use testenv.DecodeJSON instead of declaring a package-local JSON decoder.

seams.why: Temporary SQLite construction and schema stamping must share cleanup and failure behavior.
seams.remediation: Use testenv.NewSQLiteStore and testenv.StampSQLiteUserVersion instead of package-local harness functions.

seams.why: Safeguard tests must restore shared host lookup seams uniformly after every test.
seams.remediation: Use hostreqkittest.StubLookups instead of a safeguard-local snapshot helper.

seams.why: Repository layout names must come from the repository contract so consumers cannot drift independently.
seams.remediation: Use the repository contract path constants instead of a bare layout literal.
seams.reserve_reason: Extending the retrospective guard exposes 130 pre-existing layout-name literals across internal/: 80 resources, 20 internal, 16 packages, 5 .vrooli, 5 docs, 4 cmd, and 3 scenarios. The measured reserve prevents growth while migration to repocontractmeta remains successor work.

seams.why: Platform decisions must use one typed vocabulary while preserving Go and wire spellings explicitly at their boundaries.
seams.remediation: Use hostreqspec.PlatformLinux, PlatformDarwin, PlatformMacOS, PlatformWindows, or PlatformFromGOOS instead of a bare OS literal.

seams.why: Named file modes communicate permission intent and centralize security-sensitive defaults.
seams.remediation: Use the matching internal/tuning permission constant instead of a bare octal literal.

seams.why: Purpose-named duration values expose one runtime tuning surface instead of scattering magnitude literals.
seams.remediation: Add a purpose-named internal/tuning value and use it instead of an inline duration multiplication.

seams.why: Structured CLI output must use the shared renderer instead of private tab-delimited rows.
seams.remediation: Render the row through cliout instead of a multi-tab fmt.Fprintf format literal.

seams.why: Command parsing must use the shared binding surface instead of private flag sets.
seams.remediation: Migrate the command to commandtree.BindCommand.
seams.reserve_reason: Three live flag sets remain: two legacy command parsers and the commandtree compatibility constructor that owns their shared flag policy.

seams.why: Shell fixtures must use the governed runner so execution and cleanup are observable.
seams.remediation: Move the shell fixture behind shelltest.Run.

seams.why: Context deadlines need one named policy so operational timing stays reviewable.
seams.remediation: Use a named timeout from internal/tuning.

seams.why: Exact collection membership wrappers must remain on the standard-library path after helper adoption.
seams.remediation: Use slices.Contains, or document the semantic comparator and keep it outside this seam scope.

seams.why: Equivalent lexical containment checks use the shared filesystem contract so equal paths, descendants, prefix siblings, and volume errors stay consistent.
seams.remediation: Use fsx.Within for lexical containment; retain stronger resolved or authorization-specific checks when their policy differs.

seams.why: Typed JSON file round-trips share one empty-file, trailing-value, formatting, and newline contract.
seams.remediation: Use fsx.ReadJSON and fsx.MarshalJSON for equivalent typed file persistence; retain domain codecs for wire or encrypted payloads.

seams.why: Manifest discovery must distinguish absence from permission and I/O failures instead of collapsing every stat error into a missing file.
seams.remediation: Use fsx.Exists when the caller needs an existence predicate with an error channel; retain Lstat/stat metadata checks when metadata or symlink policy is the contract.

seams.why: Clock interfaces must share the one deterministic contract instead of drifting by package.
seams.remediation: Use internal/clock.Clock and testenv.NewClock.

seams.why: RFC3339 output is a wire and operator contract; the shape remains visible while non-storage adapters retain their required precision and presentation policy.
seams.remediation: Use the canonical adapter when the output contract is equivalent; retain and document a reserve for deliberate wire-format adapters.
seams.reserve_reason: The current tree has 32 deliberate RFC3339 presentation and wire-format adapters. storagetime.FormatUTC intentionally emits fixed nanosecond precision for SQLite ordering, so these sites cannot be mechanically replaced without changing contracts.

seams.why: Service-manifest dependency decoding belongs to the scenario contract owner.
seams.remediation: Use scenario.LoadServiceManifest instead of an anonymous nested decoder.

seams.why: Command-binding dialects must converge on the canonical root binder; lifecycle methods such as bindPorts are outside this semantic pattern.
seams.remediation: Use rootcli.BindService for command binding.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 named private JSON writers; command JSON belongs to the shared renderer.
seams.remediation: Use cliout.WriteJSON or a named response type.

seams.why: Dynamic protobuf JSON construction belongs at the shared output boundary.
seams.remediation: Return a named response value and render it through cliout.WriteJSONValue.

seams.why: A constant name must explain the value's role; generic linter-appeasement names preserve no more meaning than the literal they replace.
seams.remediation: Rename the constant with at least one package-domain word that states what its value controls.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 value-named duration constants.
seams.remediation: Use a purpose-named tuning duration.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 repeated stamped test names.
seams.remediation: Give each test a domain-specific name.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 stamped handler tests.
seams.remediation: Name handler tests for the behavior they verify.

seams.why: Command-binding call sites must use the canonical root binder; unrelated object methods such as bindPorts are not command binders.
seams.remediation: Bind commands through the canonical root binder.

seams.why: A file-level goconst directive silently exempts every declaration in the file; its cost must reflect that breadth.
seams.remediation: Extract a domain constant, narrow the directive to the fixture declaration, or document why the whole-file exception is irreducible.
seams.reserve_reason: The remaining fixture suppressions are explicitly justified in their directive comments; breadth pricing keeps every covered declaration visible until those fixtures are incrementally narrowed.

seams.why: Ratchet start: 67 gocyclo directives were observed; suppressions must remain explicit and reviewable.
seams.remediation: Decompose the function or document a reviewed, irreducible exception.
seams.reserve_reason: Sixty-two declaration-scoped non-test suppressions remain individually justified after decomposing three declarative command tables and deleting obsolete suppressed declarations.

seams.why: A call-name ratchet is evadable by replacing the standard-library sort with a slower private nested-swap implementation.
seams.remediation: Delete the private helper and call slices.Sort directly.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 hand-written argv dispatchers.
seams.remediation: Use the typed command tree parser and binder.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 duplicate runner interfaces.
seams.remediation: Reuse the canonical runner interface.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 duplicate LookPath fakes.
seams.remediation: Reuse the canonical shell test seam.

seams.why: Ratchet start: census observed 0 untyped boundary errors.
seams.remediation: Normalize boundary errors through vroolierr.

seams.why: Every handler directory must carry executable tests.
seams.remediation: Add a *_test.go file beside the handler implementation.

seams.why: Every safeguard handler directory must carry a conformance reference.
seams.remediation: Add a hostreq conformance test beside the handler.

seams.why: The tidiness seam engine must not silently skip when its symbol fact provider is absent.
seams.remediation: Declare code-facts as an enabled, required tidiness-manager scenario dependency.

seams.why: Generated coverage output must remain ephemeral and must not become grader source.
seams.remediation: Remove the committed coverage artifact and let test-genie regenerate it.

seams.why: Backup source files are not part of a scenario's reviewed implementation.
seams.remediation: Remove the committed test backup artifact.

seams.why: Test logs are run output and must not be committed as scenario source.
seams.remediation: Remove the committed test log artifact.

seams.why: Compiled executables outside declared build output directories are source-tree residue and must remain visible.
seams.remediation: Remove the executable artifact or emit it beneath .vrooli/build or .vrooli/bin.

seams.why: The typed root binding seam keeps command policy and renderer wiring uniform.
seams.remediation: Use rootcli.BindService or the matching typed canonical binder.

seams.why: Every credentials command that emits JSON must have a named contract assertion.
seams.remediation: Add the command function name to TestCredentialJSONContracts before adding or changing its JSON output.

seams.why: A concrete declaration in both an application domain and its CLI counterpart creates two authorities that can drift independently.
seams.remediation: Keep the concrete declaration in internal/app/<domain> and expose a type alias from the CLI package.
seams.reserve_reason: Seven successor-domain duplicates remain: hygiene Request; package RunResponse, RefreshRequest, RefreshItem, and RefreshResponse; runtime WriteSupervisorStatusJSON and WriteSupervisorServiceResultJSON. The project, scenario, and resource domains are at zero.

seams.canonical: application services independent of CLI transport
seams.why: Application packages must remain reusable by non-CLI consumers and must not own command parsing or root CLI policy.
seams.remediation: Move argument parsing, help rendering, and CLI errors into the matching internal/cli handler package; expose context-aware service methods from internal/app.
